correctness.rationale: With center and two leaves, the directed neighborhood indicators reduce exactly to 0 for center updates and (b-a)/2 for both leaf updates. Strict gate yields permanently frozen leaves at or below half the initial gap, and an iid affine center recursion; explicit contractive coupling, the SLLN and iid two-atom nonconvergence prove its asserted limits and moments. Above the gap threshold, ordered bilateral averaging preserves a shrinking gap and sum; the exact variance-drop identity and spectral/Poincare inequality yield an exponential mean-square bound, then a.s. consensus by Markov and Borel–Cantelli. Boundaries rho=1/2, epsilon=gap/2, endpoint center values were checked. Standalone exact rational tests independently recompute the oriented gate and algebra; finite checks are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The genuinely new scoped claim is the complete sharp confidence cutoff in the source pure-transitive three-node path model, not the classical Bernoulli/stubborn-agent invariant law. Source Eq. (3) and full-text results, a prior full-text stubborn-gossip example, and bounded-confidence clique results were compared by actual update implications. The older stubborn-agent model explains the low branch after reduction but not the endogenous threshold or high branch; the source manuscript studies the NDW system but not this classification. Residual possible equivalent state-dependent-gossip treatments are disclosed; the searches do not prove global uniqueness.
residual_risks: A model-specific sharp cutoff may have been derived elsewhere under terminology such as one-sided neighborhood confidence or endogenously stubborn agents; no independent bibliographic audit was performed.

value.rationale: The three-node path is the smallest connected graph with nontrivial neighbor-of-neighbor asymmetry; exact leaf-gap gating is a natural structural observable. Classifying every ordered initial state across all allowed confidence thresholds identifies an abrupt, strict-boundary change from provable averaging consensus to almost-sure persistent fluctuations despite connected social contact. The precise rate and stationary law make the boundary testable and give a mathematical benchmark for transitive-influence simulation, beyond an arbitrary numerical parameter slice or a mere sign check.
